'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#D2B1D9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#AE8BB1|50%}} {{legend0|#808080|No votes}} | title = U.S. Representative | before_election = [[George Santos]] | after_election = [[Tom Suozzi]] | after_party = Democratic Party (United States) | before_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{Elections in New York (state) sidebar}} The '''2024 New York's 3rd congressional district special election''' was held on February 13, 2024, to fill the vacant seat in [[New York's 3rd congressional district]] for the remainder of the [[118th United States Congress]]. The seat became vacant after the [[Expulsion from the United States Congress|expulsion]] of [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[George Santos]] on December 1, 2023. Considered a suburban [[marginal seat|swing seat]], political analysts predicted a competitive and expensive election for both parties.{{Cite news |last=Stewart |first=Kyle |date=December 1, 2023 |title=George Santos was expelled from the House — what happens next? |work=[[NBC News]] |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/george-santos-expelled-house-what-happens-how-rcna127518 |access-date=December 2, 2023}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.cookpolitical.com/analysis/house/new-york-house/ny-03-santos-expulsion-likely-toss-special-looms-long-island|title=NY-03: With Santos Expulsion Likely, Toss Up Special Looms on Long Island|website=The Cook Political Report|first=Dave|last=Wasserman|date=December 1, 2023}} The [[early voting]] period ran from February 3 to February 11, 2024.{{Cite web|title=Upcoming Elections 2024|url=https://vote.nyc/elections|access-date=January 24, 2024|website=Board of Elections in the City of New York}}{{Cite web|title=Special Election: February 13, 2024|url=https://www.nassaucountyny.gov/566/Board-of-Elections|access-date=January 24, 2024|website=Nassau County Board of Elections }} Republicans nominated [[Nassau County Legislature|Nassau County legislator]] [[Mazi Melesa Pilip]], while Democrats nominated [[Tom Suozzi]], the former U.S. representative for this district and Santos's predecessor. Suozzi defeated Pilip, reclaiming the seat for Democrats.{{Cite web |date=2024-02-13 |title=Democrat Tom Suozzi wins New York race to succeed George Santos in Congress |url=https://apnews.com/article/george-santos-suozzi-pilip-special-election-be0140979ca3050921579e90507bfe1f |access-date=2024-02-14 |website=AP News |language=en}} This was the first time that a New York congressional seat changed parties in a special election since [[2011 New York's 9th congressional district special election|2011]]. == Background == Republican [[George Santos]] was elected to Congress in [[2022 New York's 3rd congressional district election|2022]] from New York's 3rd district. Weeks later, ''[[The New York Times]]'' reported that he had misrepresented his background during the campaign.[https://www.nytimes.com/2022/12/19/nyregion/george-santos-ny-republicans.html Who Is Rep.-Elect George Santos? His Résumé May Be Largely Fiction.], [[New York Times]], December 19, 2022 Santos confirmed the allegations against him were true soon after, but refused to resign from his seat.[https://www.cnn.com/2022/12/26/politics/george-santos-admits-embellishing-resume/index.html Rep.-elect George Santos admits to lying about bio, but says he still intends to serve in Congress], [[CNN Politics]], December 27, 2022 After a formal inquiry by the [[United States House Committee on Ethics|House Ethics Committee]], he was [[Expulsion from the United States Congress|expelled]] from the House of Representatives on December 1, 2023, by a vote of 311 to 114. At the time of the expulsion, he was indicted on 23 federal charges related to [[fraud]].[https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/4341797-fetterman-menendez-cameo-video-santos/ Fetterman says he sent ‘ethically-challenged’ Menendez a Cameo video from Santos], The Hill Santos was the first representative to be expelled in two decades and the first since the [[American Civil War|Civil War]] to be expelled before any criminal conviction.{{Cite news |last1=Sangal |first1=Aditi |last2=Shelton |first2=Shania |date=December 1, 2023 |title=House expels GOP Rep. George Santos over ethics violations |work=[[CNN]] |url=https://www.cnn.com/politics/live-news/george-santos-expulsion-vote-12-1-23/index.html |access-date=December 2, 2023}} == Nominees== New York does not use [[Partisan primary|primary election]]s when filling vacancies. Instead, party officials in the affected counties (in this case, [[Nassau County, New York|Nassau]] and [[Queens]]) are responsible for choosing nominees.{{cite news |last1=Bowman |first1=Bridget |title=George Santos' exit sets up a competitive special election |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2024-election/george-santos-exit-sets-competitive-special-election-rcna127236 |access-date=December 1, 2023 |work=[[NBC News]] |date=December 1, 2023 |language=en}} === Democratic Party === Democrats selected [[Tom Suozzi]] as the party's nominee on December 7, 2023.{{Cite news |last1=Shepherd |first1=Bridget |last2=Bowman |date=December 7, 2023 |title= New York Democrats pick Tom Suozzi as their candidate for George Santos' seat |work=[[NBC News]] |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/new-york-democrats-pick-tom-suozzi-candidate-george-santos-seat-rcna128540 |access-date=December 7, 2023}} He had previously represented the district in the House from 2017 to 2023. Before that, he served as the [[Nassau County, New York|Nassau County]] executive and the mayor of [[Glen Cove, New York|Glen Cove]], and had run for governor in [[2006 New York gubernatorial election|2006]] and [[2022 New York gubernatorial election|2022]].{{Cite news |last1=Shepherd |first1=Bridget |last2=Bowman |date=December 7, 2023 |title=New York Democrats pick Tom Suozzi as their candidate for George Santos' seat |work=[[NBC News]] |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/elections/new-york-democrats-pick-tom-suozzi-candidate-george-santos-seat-rcna128540 |access-date=December 7, 2023}} === Republican Party === On December 14, 2023, Republicans selected [[Mazi Melesa Pilip]] as their nominee to replace Santos.{{Cite web |last=LaRocco |first=Paul |date=2023-12-14 |title=GOP picks Mazi Melesa Pilip to run in special election to replace ousted George Santos, former Rep. Pete King confirms |url=https://www.newsday.com/long-island/politics/mazi-pilip-special-election-iaxhw4an |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=Newsday |language=en}} She previously served in the [[Israel Defense Forces]], and has represented the 10th legislative district in the [[Nassau County Legislature]] since 2022.{{Cite web |date=2021-11-29 |title=This one-time refugee and former Israeli paratrooper just won a seat in her county legislature |url=https://forward.com/news/478772/this-jewish-woman-of-color-a-former-israeli-paratrooper-just-won-a-seat-in/ |access-date=2023-12-14 |website=The Forward |language=en}} She was a registered Democrat who held office as a Republican.{{Cite web|url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/news/2023/12/14/gop-nomination-mazi-melesa-pilip-george-santos-congressional-seat|title=GOP nominates Nassau legislator Mazi Pilip to run for Santos' seat|date=December 14, 2023|website=NY1|first=Bobby|last=Cuza }} === Minor parties === New York allows [[fusion voting]] in elections, prompting minor parties to nominate candidates on their ballot lines. The [[Conservative Party of New York State]] nominated Pilip.{{cite web|url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/news/2023/12/14/gop-nomination-mazi-melesa-pilip-george-santos-congressional-seat|title=GOP nominates Nassau legislator Mazi Pilip to run for Santos' seat|first=Bobby|last=Cuza|date=December 14, 2023|access-date=December 15, 2023|website=[[NY1]]}} Suozzi declined to seek the support of the
